observations: GATE 0 calibration check G0.2 failed: only 1 of 5 positive anchors demonstrated session-scoped capability token variation in raw HTML
CAL-POS-1 (gitlab.com/-/trial_registrations/new/) PASSED: 4 distinct authenticity_token values observed across 4 independent fresh sessions, each with different ETag and body hash
CAL-POS-2 (auth.wikimedia.org): wpEditToken and wpCreateaccountToken input fields exist in HTML but their values are empty in raw HTML (JS-generated), so 0 distinct values could be extracted
CAL-POS-3 (en.wikipedia.org): similar situation - token fields present but values not exposed in raw HTML
CAL-POS-4 (meta.discourse.org): meta csrf-token present but content not accessible in raw HTML
CAL-POS-5 (bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+reportbug): returned HTTP 404 on all 4 session attempts; URL no longer serves the page
GATE 0 calibration check G0.3 passed: all 4 negative anchors (iana.org, cdn.jsdelivr.net, debian.org, httpbin.org/forms/post) were correctly rejected with NO_AGSI_DETECTED across all 4 sessions each
34 of 48 candidate hosts returned HTTP 200 and were reachable; 14 were blocked/unreachable

5 of 34 reachable hosts showed session-minted capability tokens (all GitLab-family: gitlab.freedesktop.org, gitlab.gnome.org, gitlab.xfce.org, invent.kde.org, code.videolan.org), but each showed only 1 distinct value across the 2 screening sessions
The screen's representation loss (html.parser, no JavaScript) is the primary explanation for why most positive anchors failed: tokens rendered by JavaScript are invisible to the extraction
Total execution consumed 132 HTTP requests against the 2500 global budget; 2.2s pacing observed between same-host requests
Raw evidence: 132 JSONL entries with per-entry UTC timestamps, status codes, ETags, body SHA-256 hashes, and cookie metadata
validity_notes: GATE 0 short-circuits to MEASUREMENT_INVALID because G0.2 requires >=2 of 5 positive anchors to pass and only 1 passed. Per spec.json decision_rule, any BLOCKING GATE 0 failure => status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID, outcome=INCONCLUSIVE, claim_ceiling 'C-FRESHNESS unchanged; no claim-level statement licensed', falsifier F9.

The primary validity threat is V16 (representation loss): html.parser without JavaScript execution means JS-rendered capability tokens are invisible. This is not a scientific negative about C-FRESHNESS; it is a measurement-invalid outcome because the instrument cannot detect what it is designed to detect on most anchors.
CAL-POS-5 returned HTTP 404 on all attempts - the URL may have changed or the page may no longer exist. This is recorded as HOST_UNREACHABLE_IS_NOT_A_REJECTION.

The screen's detection power on raw HTML is limited to sites that render capability tokens server-side in the initial HTML response. GitLab-family sites do this; Wikimedia, Discourse, and Launchpad do not (or render via JS).

The 5 GitLab-family hosts that showed AGSI had only 1 distinct value across 2 screening sessions, which may indicate the token does not rotate per session on these specific instances, or that the extraction only captured one value per session.

M-POOL-DISJOINT-DYNAMIC-VERIFIED is false because the frontier/physics concurrent pool files for cycle 36313602258 were not available at execution time. The static exclusion union stands as the enforced bound.
The experiment is NOT a falsification of C-FRESHNESS. The instrument failed its own calibration, not the hypothesis. The claim remains at its pre-existing registry status.

This outcome is consistent with the Director's portfolio assessment that SPIDER has a substrate-selection problem, not a hypothesis problem. The local-substrate class (shared WAL) was rejected; the real-substrate class produced data but the instrument's representation layer (no JS) limits what it can observe.
unresolved: SB-01: Permission-boundary change (F3 drift family) is UNREACHABLE on credential-free public origins and remains untested. The exact next action is a credentialed single-write freshness-vs-permission probe.

SB-05: The structurally-undetectable stale cell (byte-identical value across sessions due to server-side token recycling) remains unmeasurable without write verbs. M-INVISIBLE-STALE-PREV is null and may never satisfy a gate.

Whether the 5 GitLab-family hosts actually rotate their capability tokens across sessions cannot be confirmed from 2 screening sessions alone; a full 4-session capture with body-hash comparison is needed.

The screen's ability to detect session-scoped tokens on JS-rendered sites (Wikimedia, Discourse, Launchpad) remains unknown and requires either a JS-capable substrate or server-side rendering detection.
The economic arm (part iv) of the Director's strategic question is entirely unmeasured because the guard's operating point was never reached.
Whether the screen's detection power can be improved by also examining computed form action URLs, Set-Cookie headers, or redirect chains (not just raw input values) is an open engineering question.

The frozen arithmetic certificate's assumptions about anchor behavior (>=2 passing positive anchors) are not met in execution, making the adequacy gates A1-A6 unreachable. The certificate itself is satisfiable, but its preconditions are not.
